title: Two free bodies under the field they make

key_results.statement: The joint translation $\mathcal T$ of both bodies and all field objects commutes with $C$ for both couplings: the total plane-wave label $P$ of bodies and field is conserved; the clock levels $k_1,k_2$, $C$ and $\sum_x\Phi_x$ are conserved, and the joint reflection maps $P\to-P$.

For $(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\neq0$ the translation of the bodies alone does not commute with $C$: the plane-wave label of the bodies is not conserved (the field takes the recoil); held bodies also conserve $x_i$ and $\sigma_i$.

For even $L$ and both couplings, $Q_i=(\sum_x(-1)^xP^{(i)}_x)\sigma_3^{(i)}$ commutes with $C$ (not for odd $L$); the bodies alone conserve $k_1,k_2$ and $Q_1,Q_2$, and for bodies of one type the symmetric functions $D_1+D_2$, $D_1D_2$, $Q_1+Q_2$, $Q_1Q_2$.

Held bodies (both couplings): $E(x_1,x_2)=\sigma_1M_1+\sigma_2M_2+N_f\varepsilon_0(x_1,x_2)$, $\varepsilon_0=\min\operatorname{spec}(C_1+g_1P_{x_1}+g_2P_{x_2})$, $g_i=\sigma_i\gamma_iM_i$, simple and analytic in $g_i$; position dependence only through the mutual term $M$; for one type a function of the set of the two held bodies.

Exactly, at every order in $g_i$ (lowest state, and highest state for even $L$): $M$ depends only on the ring distance, is unchanged when the two bodies exchange places, and the symmetric-difference forces satisfy $F_1=-F_2$ (action equals reaction).

For even $L$, $\mathcal W=U_f\sigma_2^{(1)}\sigma_2^{(2)}$ gives $\mathcal WC\mathcal W^\dagger=-C$: the highest field state with branches $(\sigma_1,\sigma_2)$ is the lowest with $(-\sigma_1,-\sigma_2)$, with equal accelerations from rest, and $M_{\rm top}(g_1,g_2)=-M_{\rm low}(-g_1,-g_2)$.
Second-order mutual term on the ring: $M^{(2)}(d)=\frac{n g_1g_2}{6t_fL}[6u-(L^2-1)]$, valid in the convergence domain $\lvert g_1\rvert+\lvert g_2\rvert<2t_f\sin^2(\pi/L)$.
Third-order mutual term on the ring: $M^{(3)}(d)=\frac{n g_1g_2(g_1+g_2)}{60t_f^2L^2}[20u^2-10(L^2-2)u+(L^2-1)(L^2-4)]$.
At second order the mutual term is a product $g_1g_2F_2(d)$ (same number per body for acting and being acted upon); at third order no product $p_1(g_1)p_2(g_2)F(d)+O(g^4)$ exists for $L\ge5$.

Exactly, for bodies of different types: the chart mean position $\langle\hat x_i\rangle$, $\hat x_i=\sum_x\chi_i(x)P^{(i)}_x$, satisfies $\frac{d^2}{d\lambda^2}\langle\hat x_i\rangle=\langle i[C,v_i]\rangle-L\langle i[C,v_{i*}]\rangle$, $v_i$ the winding current and $v_{i*}$ its part on the cut bond; the cut term acts only on the four places within one place of the cut.

In the adiabatic basis the effective hopping of an isolated dressed body moves it by $r\in\{0,\pm2\}$ at order $\tau^2$, and $E''_{k,\sigma}(0)=-8\bar\kappa$ is the curvature (6.10); for the highest state $E''_{\rm top,\sigma}=-E''_{{\rm low},-\sigma}$.

Regime R (isolated band, order $\tau_i^2$, real product starts), first order in the place dependence: $a_1=a_1^{(0)}-E''_{k_1,\sigma_1}(0)\sum_{j,l}\tfrac12\Delta\chi_1(j)\phi^1_{j+1}\phi^1_{j-1}(\phi^2_l)^2\partial_1W(j,l)$, $a_1^{(0)}=-\frac{L}{64}E''^2_1\Xi_1$ the free-packet cut part (order $\tau^4$), and likewise $a_2$; $W$ the exact held eigenvalue, $\partial_2W=-\partial_1W$; relative errors $O(\tau'^2/\delta_1^2)+O(\tau'^2/(\delta_1\delta))$.

For real Gaussian envelopes of widths $w_i$: $(a_1-a_1^{(0)})/(a_2-a_2^{(0)})=-(E''_1/E''_2)e^{(w_2^{-2}-w_1^{-2})/2}$, for equal widths $-\mu_2/\mu_1$ with $\mu_i=1/E''_{k_i,\sigma_i}(0)$, for the exact mutual term and to the order of (6.10), up to relative corrections at most of order $L\varpi_i\max\lvert\mathcal M'\rvert/\lvert\sum p\mathcal M'\rvert$ from the places next to the cuts.
With the rest cost $R_i=M_i(1+\gamma_in)+O(\gamma_i^3)$: $\mu_i=\sigma_iR_i/\tau_i^2+O(\gamma_i^2)$ for (a) and $\mu_i=\sigma_iR_i/[\tau_i(1+\gamma_in)]^2+O(\gamma_i^2)$ for (c).

At second order in the couplings, separations on the shorter arc, small $\gamma_in$, for the mutual parts: in the lowest field state the bodies move towards each other iff $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=\operatorname{sgn}(\gamma_1\gamma_2)$, apart iff $\sigma_1=\sigma_2=-\operatorname{sgn}(\gamma_1\gamma_2)$, in the same direction iff $\sigma_1\ne\sigma_2$; in the highest state (even $L$) with $\sigma_i\to-\sigma_i$.

At second order in the place dependence each body's hopping is changed by the other's mark by the relative amount $\mp\gamma_i\overline{\delta\rho}$ (upper sign (a), lower (c)), with $\gamma_1\delta\rho_l(y)=\sigma_1M^{(2)}(y,l)/M_1+O(g_2^2)$.

For equal-width Gaussian envelopes, at leading order in $\gamma_i$: $(a_1-a_1^{(0)})/(a_2-a_2^{(0)})=-\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_1}[1-\langle\!\langle\bar M^{(2)}\rangle\!\rangle(s_1\sigma_1/M_1-s_2\sigma_2/M_2)]$, $s_i=\pm1$ for (a)/(c), $\langle\!\langle\cdot\rangle\!\rangle$ the average weighted by $p_{jl}\mathcal M'(l-j)$: a deviation of relative order $\gamma_1\gamma_2$.

definitions.name: field coupling constant of a body
regime R of item 3 (isolated band with gaps delta_1 and delta, order tau squared, real product starts with chart centres)
adiabatic basis of the two-body band
chart mean position of a body
averaged density change made by the other body

open_issues: Out of scope by the question's note: the highest state on odd rings, and item 3 for two bodies of one type.
The coefficient of (2.16), (2.19) beyond its leading order in γ_i is not derived; the code finds relative first-order corrections in γ_i that are large for coupling (c).
R1 is assumed: for large N_f the isolation from multi-object field excitations at distance 2M_i is not derived.
Whether (2.13) holds beyond order τ² for broad starts is not derived; the free-packet part a_i^(0) is given only at its leading order τ_i⁴.
The list of conserved operators of the bodies alone is not shown to be complete.

consistency_checks.check: Dimensions of M2, M3, E'', the free-packet term and the accelerations in units of λ
Held source (τ_2 → 0) reproduces (7.7) with (7.2); test body (γ_1 → 0) falls independently of branch and level
Two types with equal parameters and mirror-symmetric starts give a_1 = -a_2
